outbreaks.title: Broader Transmission of Mpox (Clade Ib MPXV) — Global Situation
outbreaks.status: Active — PHEIC lifted 5 Sep 2025; sustained transmission continues
outbreaks.desc: WHO's 69th mpox situation report (14 September 2026) counts 52,424 laboratory-confirmed cases and 238 deaths (CFR 0.5%) across 35 African countries between 1 January 2025 and 16 August 2026; in the latest six-week window (6 Jul–16 Aug) 11 African countries had active transmission, with 1,153 confirmed cases and 7 deaths. WHO lifted the mpox PHEIC on 5 September 2025 but continues to advise emergency preparedness, and clade Ib has since caused locally acquired cases in countries across four of six WHO regions.
outbreaks.more: Madagascar has had the largest clade Ib outbreak to date (1,092 confirmed cases and 3 deaths by 19 April 2026, across 51 districts). South Africa reported 22 laboratory-confirmed cases as of 22 September 2026 (Western Cape 18, Gauteng 3, KwaZulu-Natal 1) in two clusters of close contacts, with clade Ib preliminarily involved; 13 of the Western Cape cases were confirmed since mid-August. Singapore reported its first clade Ib cases on 2 April 2026, and Estonia its first clade I case in August 2026. UK: UKHSA's 8 October overview (data to 30 September) records 226 clade Ib cases in the UK since 2023 against 972 clade IIb, and states that clade Ib cases exceeded clade IIb cases from July 2026; a recombinant Ib/IIb virus was identified in a traveller in England in October 2025. No WHO situation report newer than #69 (14 September) was located.
outbreaks.src: WHO mpox external situation report #69 (14 Sep 2026) via NICD; NICD South Africa mpox update (22 Sep 2026); WHO situation report #65 (Apr 2026); WHO DON-587; NaTHNaC; UKHSA Mpox outbreak epidemiological overview, 8 Oct 2026

outbreaks.title: Measles Outbreak — Bangladesh
outbreaks.status: Active — world's largest current measles outbreak (per CDC)
outbreaks.desc: Bangladesh's Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reported 188,041 suspected and 21,212 laboratory-confirmed measles cases and 1,096 deaths (995 among suspected cases, 101 among confirmed cases) in 2026 up to 8 am on 27 September — up from 1,009 deaths on 9–10 September. ECDC's week-41 report (October) cites a newer, higher case count — 201,625 suspected and 22,116 confirmed cases — but a lower death figure (1,040); the two series appear to use different definitions or cut-off dates and have not been reconciled, so deaths should be read as roughly 1,040–1,100. It is the country's deadliest measles outbreak in decades (Bangladesh recorded 132 cases and no deaths in all of 2025), and CDC lists it as the world's largest current measles outbreak. The emergency measles-rubella campaign that began 5 April vaccinated roughly 18–19.75 million children against an 18 million target, but about four million children were missed; DGHS acknowledged herd immunity was not achieved and says a further campaign is being prepared.
outbreaks.more: WHO and UNICEF link the crisis to gaps in Bangladesh's immunization programme that emerged in 2024–2025 after the political upheaval; the Health Minister told parliament in September that procurement-policy changes in that period created a vaccine shortage. Dhaka hospitals report overcrowded wards, and chronic child malnutrition is raising case fatality. 79% of early cases were in children under five (WHO DON-598, April 2026). No official figures newer than 10 September were located as of 28 September.
outbreaks.src: IANS/UNB relaying DGHS, 27 Sep 2026; ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report week 41 (7 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera, 9 & 14 Sep 2026 (citing DGHS); AFP, 9–10 Sep 2026; WHO DON-598 (Apr 2026)

outbreaks.title: Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute — Technician Death, Suspected Lab Exposure (Russia)
outbreaks.status: Unconfirmed — official cause "pneumonia of undetermined etiology"; WHO seeking to verify
outbreaks.desc: Darya Shipilova, 28, a technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, was hospitalised on 29 September and died in the night of 1–2 October in a hospital in Shelekhov. Local and independent Russian media (People of Baikal, citing unnamed sources) report she broke a test tube containing pneumonic-plague bacteria (Yersinia pestis) on 25 September; Russian authorities have not confirmed this. Governor Igor Kobzev, citing a Rospotrebnadzor inspection and an expert commission, says the cause was pneumonia of undetermined etiology; Rospotrebnadzor says no microorganisms linked to her work were found in her samples and no high-threat pathogen was identified, and that no pathogen accidents are recorded at the institute. Russia's update to WHO (received 6 October) states that no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk city. Rospotrebnadzor also called a circulating document describing special anti-plague measures 'untrue'.
outbreaks.more: Contacts and containment: roughly 189–200 contacts were placed under observation or isolation; ECDC reports all tested negative at the time of reporting. Rospotrebnadzor reported two COVID and two rhinovirus cases among contacts and no other infectious cases. The governor says no other institute staff have sought medical care since the death and that the situation is stable. Reports from anonymous sources of more than 60 staff confined on site, and of hospital wards cordoned off and a mask mandate at the Irkutsk Aluminum Plant (3 October), come from media and are not officially confirmed. WHO (spokesman Christian Lindmeier, 7 October) rates the risk as moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia and very low for the rest of Europe, and says it is seeking to verify the event and the laboratory tests. UKHSA rates the risk to the UK as very low. US officials (Trump, Rubio) say they are monitoring closely; Rubio urged Russia to share more information. An international plague conference scheduled in Irkutsk for 21–22 October was arranged in June, according to the organisers. There is no public evidence of spread to residents and none linking the death to a weapons programme. Treat the plague-exposure account as UNCONFIRMED: it rests on Russian media and anonymous sources, and the official position is that the cause is undetermined.
outbreaks.src: AFP via Courthouse News, 6 Oct 2026; ECDC CDTR week 41 (7 Oct 2026); UKHSA Outbreaks under monitoring week 40; RFE/RL; Al Jazeera, 6 Oct 2026; Gulf News/AP, 5 Oct 2026; CBS News

outbreaks.title: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) — DRC / Uganda
outbreaks.status: PHEIC · Active — largest recorded Bundibugyo outbreak; first imported case in Kenya (6 Oct)
outbreaks.desc: As of data to 6 October 2026 (reported 7 October, ECDC), DRC has 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths, with 1,066 patients hospitalized in isolation and 2,269 recovered, across seven provinces and 64 of 167 health zones. The latest daily report added 63 cases and 27 deaths, and 82% of identified contacts are under follow-up. By province (cases/deaths): Ituri 6,513/3,007; North Kivu 1,785/1,021; Haut-Uélé 364/153; Tshopo 51/18; Bas-Uélé 10/4; South Kivu 3/1; Sud Ubangi 2/1. UKHSA's week-40 report (data to 4 October: 8,603 cases, 4,148 deaths) counted 487 new cases and 224 deaths in the week and notes North Kivu is rising. Compared with 7,890 cases and 3,799 deaths on 23 September, that is roughly 840 more cases and 400 more deaths in two weeks. WHO assesses the risk as very high in DRC, high in bordering countries, and low elsewhere; UKHSA rates the risk to the UK as low. The PHEIC was declared on 17 May 2026 and remains in force after the second IHR Emergency Committee (18 August).
outbreaks.more: KENYA — first imported case: Kenya's Health Ministry confirmed on 6 October a Bundibugyo case in a Kenyan citizen who had lived in DRC for seven years, fell ill about a month earlier, travelled by road to Kampala and flew to Nairobi on 3 October. He was isolated on arrival and died on 5 October. Kenya reports 28 contacts identified and 23 passengers and 4 crew from the flight being traced, and says it has screened 652,584 travellers since enhanced surveillance began. OTHER SPREAD: Uganda's outbreak (20 confirmed cases, 2 deaths) was declared over in late August (sources give 25 or 27 August). A DRC-based health worker (MSF) tested positive on 29 September and was admitted in Leiden on 1 October; UKHSA counts this as the fourth imported case in Europe, after France (a doctor, 24 June), Germany (US citizens medevaced in May and July) and a UK evacuation (July). CDC stated earlier that no cases had been confirmed in the United States; no newer statement was located. COUNTERMEASURES: there is still no licensed Bundibugyo vaccine or therapy. On 31 July WHO's advisory group recommended prioritising the Zaire-species vaccine Ervebo for a Phase 3 trial (reversing its May position); the International Coordinating Group released 70,000 doses to DRC (20,000 for the trial, 50,000 for frontline workers) and a vaccination campaign for frontline workers began in Kisangani on 27 August (ECDC). Africa CDC noted there is no reliable evidence of efficacy against Bundibugyo yet. Moderna's mRNA-1469 entered a Phase 1 trial on 4 August; the PARTNERS trial (MBP134 and remdesivir) had enrolled 200 participants by late August; WHO has listed two more diagnostics for emergency use. Armed conflict, weak infrastructure and unpaid health-worker salaries continue to hamper the response, and the true scale is likely higher than confirmed counts.
outbreaks.src: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report week 41 (7 Oct 2026); UKHSA Outbreaks under monitoring, week 40 (to 4 Oct 2026); Capital FM Kenya, 6 Oct 2026; Anadolu/AJC/ABC News on Kenya case, 6 Oct 2026; IPP Secretariat Day-100 countermeasures tracker (25 Aug 2026); WHO DON-617

outbreaks.title: MERS-CoV — Global Update
outbreaks.desc: ECDC's update published 5 October 2026 (totals to 29 September) shows no change from August: 2,649 cases and 960 deaths since April 2012, with two cases (one death) reported in 2026, all in Saudi Arabia (as of 31 August). New cases detected through surveillance are at their lowest level since 2014, and ECDC assesses the risk to the EU/EEA as low. WHO EMRO's June 2026 tally (2,637 cases, 965 deaths) differs slightly, reflecting reporting cutoffs and retrospective corrections. For context, 2025 saw 19 cases and 4 deaths globally, including two travel-associated cases in France.
outbreaks.src: ECDC MERS-CoV worldwide overview (published 5 Oct 2026, totals to 29 Sep); WHO EMRO MERS update, Jun 2026; WHO DON-591 (Dec 2025)

outbreaks.title: Avian & Zoonotic Influenza at the Human–Animal Interface — WHO Monthly Summary
outbreaks.desc: WHO's 6 September 2026 human–animal interface summary records, for 8 August–6 September, one new human A(H5N1) case, three A(H9N2) cases (all reported by China; two in children under five and one aged 5–10) and two A(H1N2) variant swine-influenza cases. There is no sustained human-to-human transmission and WHO's assessment of overall risk remains low. In the first quarter of 2026 WHO tracked 13 avian and swine influenza human cases, including one previously unreported fatal H5N1 case in a child in Bangladesh.
outbreaks.more: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b continues to circulate in wild birds, poultry and (in the US) dairy cattle; CDC reports sporadic human cases among US dairy and poultry workers. More than 880 sporadic human H5N1 infections have been reported to WHO since 2003. Cambodia reported its sixth human H5N1 case of 2026 on 28 September (a 49-year-old poultry farmer in Oddar Meanchey province, hospitalised; close contacts offered oseltamivir); Cambodia had 18 cases and 9 deaths in 2025 (UKHSA). A WHO human–animal interface summary newer than 6 September was not located.
outbreaks.src: WHO influenza human-animal interface summary, 6 Sep 2026; CIDRAP, 29 Apr 2026; CDC H5 bird flu situation summary; WHO/Our World in Data H5N1 series; UKHSA Outbreaks under monitoring week 40 (28 Sep Cambodia report); The Star (Malaysia), 28 Sep 2026

outbreaks.title: Cholera — West and Central Africa (Multi-country)
outbreaks.desc: ECDC's latest monthly overview (as of 28 September 2026) counts 249,136 cholera cases and 1,970 deaths worldwide since 1 January 2026 — about 43% fewer cases and 56% fewer deaths than the same point in 2025 (436,268 cases and 4,449 deaths). In the latest period (26 Aug–28 Sep) 46,153 new cases and 140 new deaths were reported, against 42,717 cases and 257 deaths in the previous period (plus 2,080 reported retrospectively). The largest contributors were Afghanistan (34,378 cases, 10 deaths), DRC (8,505 cases, the most deaths at 107), Yemen (1,885), Angola (748) and Congo (299). Nigeria, which dominated the August update, is no longer among the top five for the latest period, which suggests part of that August figure was backlog reporting. Country figures use different reporting cut-off dates.
outbreaks.more: Regional detail from UNICEF/WHO (12 Aug): cholera was active across six countries in two corridors — the Lake Chad Basin (Chad, Cameroon, Nigeria) and the Congo River Basin (DRC, Republic of Congo, CAR). Seasonal rains, flooding, displacement and cross-border movement accelerate spread; children are disproportionately affected. In DRC, cholera is occurring alongside the Ebola emergency in the east and the DRC death toll (107 in the latest period) is the highest of any country. UNICEF sought $15 million to scale up its six-month response.
outbreaks.src: ECDC Cholera Worldwide Overview (28 Sep 2026); UNICEF/UN News, 12 Aug 2026

outbreaks.title: H1N1 (Seasonal Influenza) — Delhi, India
outbreaks.desc: Delhi's H1N1 count has plateaued rather than kept accelerating: 1,777 confirmed cases as of 20 August remains the most recent Delhi Health Department cumulative figure (a 7 September ministerial statement cited 1,349, reflecting a different reporting cutoff, not a decline). Of 2,392 influenza A cases recorded to 20 August, 1,777 were H1N1, 138 H3, 37 H1 (subtype not further specified) and 440 other influenza A; a further 210 were influenza B. H1N1 has displaced H3N2 as the leading subtype this year. ICMR states that no new or more virulent strain is circulating and that circulating viruses match the Northern Hemisphere vaccine strains.
outbreaks.more: An ICMR-led virological analysis reported in New Microbes and New Infections (via a secondary summary) identifies an A/Missouri/11/2025(H1N1)pdm09-like variant within the established pdm09 lineage — not a novel reassortant. Officially, there are still zero confirmed H1N1 deaths in Delhi; the government continues to dispute media reports of fatalities. No official case count newer than 7 September was located as of 28 September; India's post-monsoon influenza peak (August–October) is a recognised seasonal pattern.
outbreaks.src: Delhi Health Dept data via Newskarnataka, 23 Aug 2026; Outlook India, 21 Aug 2026; ICMR statements; bioengineer.org summary of New Microbes and New Infections, Sep 2026; Health Minister statement via Nova Hospital Meerut, 7 Sep 2026

outbreaks.title: Cholera Outbreak — Myanmar
outbreaks.desc: A cholera outbreak has killed at least three people in Myanmar and hospitalized hundreds more with diarrhea — one death in Yangon, two in Sittwe (Rakhine State) — straining a health system already affected by civil war and economic disruption. A separate, smaller outbreak from the West/Central Africa cluster tracked above. ECDC counts only 272 cases in Myanmar as of 22 June 2026 (versus 1,888 at the same point in 2025), so this is a much smaller outbreak than last year's.
outbreaks.src: Bloomberg, 18 Aug 2026; ECDC Cholera Worldwide Overview

outbreaks.title: Andes Hantavirus — Cruise Ship (M/V Hondius), Multi-country
outbreaks.desc: Fifth and reportedly final DON on this cluster. Following notification 2 May of severe acute respiratory illness aboard, 13 cases confirmed/probable across passengers and crew (147 aboard), including 3 deaths (23% CFR). A probable case in Tristan da Cunha was later lab-confirmed after disembarkation.
outbreaks.more: CDC assessed overall US public risk as extremely low throughout; coordination extended to State Department travel guidance for affected Americans.
outbreaks.src: WHO DON-611, DON-599; CDC HAN-528/529

outbreaks.title: Nipah Virus — Kerala, India (June 2026)
outbreaks.status: Monitoring — single case, no secondary transmission reported
outbreaks.desc: Kerala's health department confirmed a laboratory-confirmed Nipah case in an adult male in Kozhikode district on 11 June 2026 (symptom onset 30 May; hospitalized 10 June with neurological manifestations and on ventilatory support in intensive care). As of 18 June, 104 contacts — including health and care workers — were under monitoring with no secondary cases, and as of 23 June there was still no evidence of secondary transmission. April–September is Kerala's recognised Nipah high-alert period; roughly a dozen confirmed cases have been reported in Kerala over the past five years.
outbreaks.more: Kerala has had recurrent Nipah spillover since 2018 (2019, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025), typically single cases or small clusters contained quickly by state and central rapid-response teams. This event is separate from the January 2026 West Bengal healthcare-worker cluster tracked above.
outbreaks.src: WHO DON-609, 25 Jun 2026; npj Viruses, May 2026

outbreaks.title: Infant Formula Contaminated with Cereulide Toxin — Multi-country
outbreaks.desc: WHO reported that precautionary recalls of infant formula linked to cereulide (a heat-stable Bacillus cereus toxin) spanned 99 countries and territories, with 144 suspected and confirmed illnesses in ten countries between 1 January and 25 February 2026; Belgium is the only country with laboratory-confirmed cases (8). Investigations point to arachidonic acid (ARA) oil used as a formula ingredient as the likely source, but a complete root-cause analysis and batch traceability had not been established. WHO rated the overall public-health risk moderate; ECDC and EFSA later concluded that, because of the recalls, the current likelihood of exposure is low, with most affected infants mildly ill and some hospitalized for dehydration.
outbreaks.more: EFSA published a rapid risk assessment on 2 February 2026 deriving an acute reference dose and action levels that Belgium and others adopted for recall decisions. In July 2026 the US FDA pressed infant-formula makers to tighten supplier oversight after this event and two separate US infant-botulism outbreaks (ByHeart, Nara Organics), all traced to ingredient supply chains rather than home handling.
outbreaks.src: WHO via Food Safety Magazine, 19 Mar 2026; ECDC/EFSA rapid outbreak assessment, Feb 2026; EFSA, 2 Feb 2026; Contemporary Pediatrics (FDA letter), 13 Jul 2026

outbreaks.title: Mpox — Recombinant Clade Ib/IIb Virus, Global
outbreaks.desc: WHO DON flags a recombinant mpox virus carrying genomic elements of both clade Ib and clade IIb — a genetic-mixing signal of concern for surveillance systems tracking lineage-specific countermeasures.
outbreaks.src: WHO DON, 14 Feb 2026

outbreaks.title: Nipah Virus — Bangladesh
outbreaks.desc: Seasonal Nipah reporting period; date-palm-sap transmission remains the primary route under investigation.
outbreaks.src: WHO DON, 6 Feb 2026

outbreaks.title: Nipah Virus — India
outbreaks.desc: In January 2026 two healthcare workers at a private hospital in Barasat (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal) were laboratory-confirmed with Nipah virus at NIV Pune. The probable index patient, a 55-year-old woman who had consumed raw date-palm sap, died. Sequencing matched Bangladesh 2022-lineage strains at 99% identity, consistent with nosocomial transmission. More than 190 contacts tested negative, aided by an NIV Pune mobile BSL-3 laboratory. WHO assesses the risk as low.
outbreaks.src: WHO DON-593 (India notification, 26 Jan 2026); npj Viruses, May 2026

outbreaks.title: Marburg Virus Disease — Ethiopia (closed)
outbreaks.desc: Outbreak declared over after two incubation periods (42 days) with no new cases. Final tally: 19 cases (14 confirmed, 5 probable), 14 deaths. 857 contacts completed monitoring. An earlier DON on the same outbreak was issued 21 Nov 2025.
outbreaks.src: WHO DON-592; earlier DON 21 Nov 2025

governance.title: CRS Update: Congress Weighs Several AI–Biosecurity Bills; Synthesis-Screening Framework Still Unrevised
governance.desc: A Congressional Research Service primer updated 15 September 2026 states that no federal law broadly regulates AI in the biological sciences and that OSTP has not revised the 2024 nucleic-acid synthesis screening framework, despite EO 14292. It lists pending bills: H.R. 3029 (Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act, passed the House); S. 3741 (Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act of 2026); S. 4363 (Engineering Biology Readiness Act); S. 4069 (AI-Ready Bio-Data Standards Act); S. 3952 (Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026); and H.R. 9307 / S. 4770 (Web of Biological Data Act of 2026). It also notes NIST's warning that AI-designed sequences could evade current screening tools, and that Anthropic reported in September that some users circumvented its biosafety safeguards while describing them as 'working scientists'. Source: a secondary summary of the CRS text; individual bill status was not independently checked on Congress.gov.

governance.title: NTI | bio Releases First Proactive Input-Screening Tool for AI Protein-Design Models
governance.desc: NTI | bio published a first-of-its-kind proof-of-concept input-screening method for AI-enabled protein-design tools — screening what goes INTO a biological AI model, rather than only screening synthesis orders on the way out. Directly responds to the finding (tracked in this tool's AI-Bio module) that open protein-design tools currently have almost no equivalent guardrails to those applied to DNA synthesis orders.

governance.title: OpenAI "Biodefense in the Intelligence Age" action plan
governance.desc: An action plan for AI-powered biological resilience, published alongside OpenAI's own biodefense summit — positions frontier labs as active participants in defensive biosecurity infrastructure, not just sources of dual-use risk.

governance.title: China's National Health Development Plan — AI-Pharma Provisions
governance.desc: China's National Health Development Plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan Period, officially released 7 Jul 2026, explicitly proposes promoting AI-enabled upgrading across the entire pharmaceutical industry value chain. Chinese regulators are concurrently building a multi-layered regulatory framework spanning data, algorithms, cybersecurity, biosafety, and healthcare regulation for this expansion.

governance.title: US Policy for Stopping High-Risk Life Sciences Research
governance.desc: Prohibits federally funded dangerous gain-of-function (DGOF) research and establishes new review requirements for potential DGOF research and international research of concern (IROC). Supersedes an earlier DURC/PEPP policy consolidation before it took effect. Per a 16 Jul 2026 Congressional Research Service report, this policy did NOT revise or replace the 2024 Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening — the separate 90-day synthesis-screening revision mandated by EO 14292 remains, per CRS, unconfirmed as fulfilled.

governance.title: Coalition Open Letter Calls for Mandatory (Not Voluntary) Synthesis Screening
governance.desc: A coalition of life-sciences researchers, AI companies, and biotechnology developers issued an open letter calling on Congress to make synthetic nucleic acid order screening legally mandatory, placing enforceable responsibility on DNA synthesis companies rather than relying on the current voluntary/self-governance model (IGSC, IBBIS Common Mechanism).

governance.title: Anthropic Proposes Government Accountability Framework for Frontier AI
governance.desc: Anthropic released a proposed policy framework recommending that frontier AI developers test models for catastrophic risks (including biological), publish findings, and be held accountable to a government agency — a call for external, not just self-imposed, oversight of the risk categories it and OpenAI both now publish internal assessments on.

governance.title: WHO Pandemic Agreement: PABS Annex Not Agreed; Negotiations Extended to May 2027
governance.desc: WHO Member States failed to agree the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) annex to the Pandemic Agreement at the IGWG session of 27 April–1 May 2026, and agreed to extend negotiations; the annex is now expected to be resubmitted no later than the World Health Assembly in May 2027, with a further IGWG session held 6–17 July 2026. The main divide is between many developing and emerging economies (including the Africa Group and the Group for Equity) and several industrialised countries, including EU Member States. Relevance: pathogen-sample and sequence sharing rules are the mechanism the Agreement relies on for outbreaks such as Bundibugyo Ebola. Outcome of the July session was not located.

governance.title: OpenAI Publishes Governance Framework Covering CBRN Risk
governance.desc: OpenAI published a governance framework describing its risk assessment and mitigation processes across four categories: cyber offense; chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) risks; harmful manipulation; and loss of control. Includes an active bounty program of up to $50,000 for researchers who find jailbreaks of ChatGPT's biosafety safeguards specifically.

governance.title: Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act (S.3741) introduced
governance.desc: Introduced in the US Senate; read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

governance.title: S.3741 Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act Introduced (Cotton–Klobuchar)
governance.desc: Bipartisan Senate bill that would direct the Secretary of Commerce to promulgate regulations on nucleic-acid synthesis security, making gene-synthesis order and customer screening a mandatory, federally enforceable near-term stopgap while a broader biosecurity strategy is developed (with exemptions for clearly non-hazardous sequences). As of the early-2026 commentary reviewed, it had not advanced beyond introduction. Update: a CRS primer (15 Sep 2026) still lists S. 3741 among pending bills.

governance.title: IBBIS International Standards Initiative launched (Singapore)
governance.desc: Meeting convened stakeholders from industry, government, academia and standards bodies to push consistent global adoption of DNA synthesis screening.

governance.title: EU Biotech Act — Biosecurity & Biodefence Provisions (Pillar 7)
governance.desc: European Commission legislative proposal COM(2025) 1022, Pillar 7, amends multiple existing EU health and food regulations to boost biodefence and biosecurity and help prevent biotechnology misuse. Stakeholder consultation (14 May–11 Jun 2025) gathered 222 contributions from industry, NGOs, and public authorities.

governance.title: Russian MFA Statement on AI-Enabled Biological Risk (BWC Conference)
governance.desc: At a BWC 50th-anniversary conference held in New Delhi, Russia's Deputy Director-General for Non-Proliferation and Arms Control formally flagged that new AI models could enable researchers to design a wider range of molecules/proteins, modify microorganisms to be undetectable, and develop new bioagents and toxins — calling for export-control attention to dual-use gene-editing platforms. References Russia's own recurring Sochi biosecurity forum (Rospotrebnadzor + MFA, most recently 10–11 Jun 2025).

governance.title: Executive Order 14292
governance.desc: Directs revision or replacement of the 2024 OSTP nucleic-acid synthesis screening framework.

governance.title: OSTP Screening Framework takes effect for purchases
governance.desc: Nucleic acid synthesis screening becomes a live requirement for purchases (condition of federal life-sciences research funding).

governance.title: India's Biosecurity Governance Gap (documented, not yet acted on)
governance.desc: ORF's 'Biosecurity blueprint for India' documents that India has no dedicated biosecurity-specific law or agency — biological risk is currently governed only through general instruments (Environment Protection Act 1986, WMD Act 2005, Biosafety Rules 1989/rDNA Guidelines 2017), which address biosafety and non-proliferation but not biosecurity as a distinct function. ORF recommends a dedicated biosecurity agency, drawing on the US's NSCEB model. This gap remains undocumented as closed as of this tracker's last check — tracked here as a standing recommendation, not a completed action.

governance.title: IBBIS Common Mechanism launched
governance.desc: Free, open-source, globally available DNA/RNA synthesis screening software released.

governance.title: OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening issued
governance.desc: Established as a voluntary-turned-conditional requirement tied to federal life-sciences funding eligibility.

governance.title: IBBIS founded as independent Swiss foundation
governance.desc: Incubated out of NTI | bio; headquartered Geneva.

governance.title: HHS voluntary synthesis-screening guidance
governance.desc: Baseline (non-binding) starting point for US gene-synthesis screening policy.
